items.text: Reza Pahlavi stated on the anniversary of 9/11 that Iranians and Americans have never been enemies and that freedom is a shared value. He identified Islamic extremism as a common enemy that has held his country hostage. He also emphasized that freedom is the foundation of America and the goal Iranians are fighting for today.
A video shows heavy vehicles in Karaj standing in a long queue to receive diesel fuel. The video was received by Iran International. The queue situation in Karaj is depicted.

Narendra Modi, the Prime Minister of India, met and talked with Masoud Pezeshkian, the head of the Islamic Republic government, on Friday, 20 Shahrivar, in Delhi. The meeting took place on the sidelines of the annual BRICS member countries summit. The topics discussed in the meeting were not disclosed.

A video has been released showing Shoja Khalilzadeh insulting several players of the Tractor team. The Football Federation's disciplinary committee last week suspended Khodadad Azizi for four months due to insults. Khalilzadeh has a history of offensive behavior towards rival teams' fans.

Pouria Bakhtiari stated that during Ebrahim Raisi's government, he was asked to teach economic topics to Raisi. These teachings were prepared as short texts for animation and cartoon production. The content was designed to be under three minutes because Raisi's mind is fleeting.

According to TankerTrackers, the total crude oil exports of Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, UAE, and Oman from the US blockade line exceeded 10 million barrels per day for the first time in two months. This increase occurred after the practical halt of the Islamabad agreement. Iran's crude oil exports remain at zero.

The US State Department's "Rewards for Justice" program announced it has set rewards of up to $10 million for information on a number of senior al-Qaeda leaders based in Iran. The program said these individuals use Iran as a safe haven for planning and executing attacks against the US and its allies. In the published poster, rewards ranging from $3 million to $10 million have been set for information on some of these individuals, and people have been asked to provide their information.

The president of the 14th government, during his visit to India, acknowledged that US pressures on Iran have reached a 'difficult and dangerous' stage. He described the world as being at one of its 'most complex junctures' and called for 'operational cooperation' among BRICS member states.

A video shows that on Friday, 20 Shahrivar, at a gathering of Iranians living in Hanover, Germany, some supporters of Palestine were also present. Police formed a line between the two groups. This event took place at the gathering site.

In the past week, 92 illegal hunters and wood traffickers were arrested. Air pollution in some cities reached very unhealthy levels, and several fires occurred in pastures and protected areas. Additionally, a decline in the Asiatic cheetah population and extensive fish deaths in the Zayandeh Rud river were reported.

Jamshid Barzegar said the September 11 attacks changed US foreign policy and global developments. Fighting terrorist groups and the Islamic Republic has become a priority for Washington. Linking the anniversary of September 11 to the current war against the Islamic Republic indicates the continuation of the counter-terrorism strategy.
Videos sent to Iran International show a large fire in the Ashkan mountains in the south of Noorabad, Mamasani on Friday, September 11.

Reza Najafi, Iran's representative to the IAEA, said the US might use the new IAEA resolution to escalate conflicts and start military operations against Iran. He called the IAEA's decision to refer Iran's case to the UN Security Council political and stated that Iran's cooperation with the agency continues. Najafi emphasized that Iran will decide its response after assessing the resolution's consequences.

An Anthropic researcher resigned due to fears about the future of artificial intelligence. He warns that a self-improving superintelligence could become a threat to human survival within this decade. He also raised questions about who should decide how and where this technology is used if even its creators are uncertain about controlling it.
The mother of Matin Montazer-ozur distributed food in memory of her killed son. Matin Montazer-ozur was 32 years old and from Gorgan. He was shot dead on January 7, 2026, in the city of Shahroud.

Daily wage workers of Bampur municipality reported non-payment of about six months' wages and non-deposit of insurance for the past year. Municipality officials have threatened workers with dismissal if they protest the situation.

A citizen posted a video showing a queue of heavy vehicles at the Chabahar cargo terminal. He says the 250-liter gasoline quota is sold for eight million tomans. Also, they have to wait in line for hours to get the quota.

Hadi Choopan, former Mr. Olympia champion, said in a video interview that he tried for 10 years to help Hani Rambod grow. He added that he never thought the day would come when Hani Rambod would be the reason for his downfall.

Aban and Hassan Mousavi, siblings arrested in connection with the December 2025 protests, are spending their 200th day in temporary detention at Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad. They face charges of moharebeh and remain in judicial uncertainty. So far, temporary release on bail has not been granted to them.

A birthday ceremony for Fathollah Avari was held at his gravesite. Fathollah Avari was one of the detainees from December 2025 who was executed on June 3, 2026. This news is based on a video received by Iran International.

Esmail Baghai, spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, stated that the Strait of Hormuz is under full control of the Islamic Republic's armed forces. He mentioned that after the Islamabad agreement, the security situation improved but the US violated the agreement. Additionally, negotiations between the Islamic Republic and Oman regarding the Strait of Hormuz are ongoing.

The US Central Command announced that American forces have redirected 99 commercial ships by September 10 to ensure the enforcement of the naval blockade against Iran. The USS Boxer and the Boxer amphibious group are involved in this operation. An image of a US Navy MH-60R Seahawk helicopter has been released.
In the audio version of Harf Akhar with Pouria Zeraati, the issue of several Islamic Republic officials contacting Mossad to eliminate Mojtaba was discussed.

Ali Abdollahi, Chief of Staff of the Iranian Armed Forces, stated that the US military has warned Iranian oil tankers to evacuate. He warned that any attack on these tankers would lead to targeting US bases in the region. These statements were made on social media.

A group of farmers in Saruno village, Kermanshah province, protested against land expropriation for a railway project. They demanded clarification of land status, fair valuation of land prices, and immediate payment of damages. The protest took place on Tuesday, September 7.

Reuters reported, citing a US official, that a US Navy ROV suffered a technical malfunction while surveying regional waters in support of operations related to the Iran war. The US official added that the ROV was an older model and did not carry any classified sonar or radar equipment.

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, is leading a new operation against the economy of the Islamic Republic, which he has called 'economic exclusion' and described as the toughest sanctions in history.

A young shopkeeper announced in a video that he is closing his shop and expressed concern about his situation. He said if he speaks out, he is labeled a foreign mercenary. This video was published on social media.

Ali Shabib, a reporter for Al-Manar network, encountered an explosion on September 6 while preparing for a live broadcast in Nabatieh, reportedly caused by an Israeli attack. In this incident, Shabib and Mohammad Barjawi, the cameraman, were injured. Released images show the explosion and their injuries.

The mother of Erfan Rezaei, a protester killed in the December 2025 protests, lit a candle on her son's tombstone. She said she lit the candle on her own birthday. The mother expressed pride in being the mother of a hero like Erfan.

Georgi Gvelesiani, former player of Persepolis and the Georgian national team, announced the end of his professional career. He spoke about playing with chronic knee injuries and fighting until the last moment. Gvelesiani thanked his fans and companions and left the football field with pride.

The Israeli Prime Minister's Office denied the UAE's warning about the October 7 attack. The office stated that if such information existed, it would have been transmitted through intelligence channels. Haaretz had reported that the UAE warned Netanyahu before the attack.

Heavy and torrential rainfall on the early morning of Tuesday, September 7, caused flooding in streets and public areas in northern Iran. The intensity was higher in some areas, leading to traffic disruptions. Rising runoff and river levels have increased concerns about potential damage in vulnerable locations.
Saudi Civil Defense announced that the warning system has been activated in Jazan, Abha, and Najran. No further details have been provided at the time of the report.

The daughter of Asieh Ramazani joined the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory" and lit a candle for her mother. She commemorated her mother and other victims of the December protests. Her mother was killed by a direct gunshot while trying to claim her rights.

The mother of Sepehr Ebrahimi, a protester killed in the December 2025 protests, released a video saying her son found peace. She added that other mothers also neither forgive nor forget. The video was shared as part of the "One Candle, One Name, One Memory" campaign.

Nader Mohammadi assisted Spartak Kastroma's first goal in the Russian Cup with a long throw-in. This was his third assist with a throw-in in the past month. Spartak Kastroma won 2-0 against Ryazan and advanced to the next round.

The coalition spokesperson against the Houthis announced that the rebels targeted civilian and economic facilities in several Saudi cities. Najran and Jazan were among the targeted areas. Maryam Rahmati from Iran International reported on the reactions to these attacks.

Active and retired railway workers in Iran gathered in front of the Ministry of Roads and Urban Development on Tuesday, September 7. They protested against low salaries and benefits. The gathering was held to express dissatisfaction with their pay conditions.

The US Treasury Department added 28 Iranian airlines, including Ata, Iran Airtour, Aseman, Kish, and Qeshm, and seven aviation-related companies to its sanctions list. Several companies based in the UAE, Britain, Turkey, Malaysia, and Kazakhstan with ties to Mahan Air or its associated networks were also sanctioned.

Scott Bessent, US Treasury Secretary, announced that as part of Operation Economic Exclusion, companies still supporting Mahan Air have been sanctioned. He added that all other Iranian airlines were also sanctioned today, and warned that cooperation with them could lead to losing access to the global financial system.

Mohammad Amin Salami's brother called on the families of the deceased to remain steadfast in keeping the memory of their loved ones alive. This message was released following reports of suicides among some family members of the deceased. Mohammad Amin Salami, 26, was killed in Kermanshah.

Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, described the Houthis as Iran's proxy. He stated that the Iranian government's involvement is clearly seen behind part of this issue. He also mentioned that the US has very strong military relations with Saudi Arabia.

A teacher sent a video to Iran International showing support for the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory." He expressed condolences to the families of the missing and encouraged them to persevere. The teacher called on the families to remain strong and be the motivation to continue the path.

France Football magazine and UEFA announced the list of 30 nominees for the 2026 Ballon d'Or. Lionel Messi is included while Cristiano Ronaldo is absent. The award ceremony will be held on October 26, 2026, in London.

A worker sent a video to Iran International showing that the cost of five daily items equals the wage for 12 hours of his work. The video highlights the economic situation of workers. The topic concerns living costs and wages.

A video shows a protester writing the slogan "Long live the Shah" on walls at night in the alleys of Torbat Heydariyeh. This incident took place in Khorasan Razavi province. The video was released by Iran International.

Iran International obtained two confidential letters from the Ministry of Oil. The letters reveal that a senior intelligence figure acting as a special assistant to the oil minister sold Iranian oil at a discount to four oil brokers. These brokers have billion-dollar debts.

US President Donald Trump, referring to the war with Iran, said the US has struck them hard and the blockade has been very powerful and effective. He also said Iran will never have nuclear weapons and has been severely punished.

Reza Pahlavi called on Iranian psychologists and therapists to provide immediate and confidential support to the families of the missing. He also urged compatriots to visit and support these families. Recently, a justice-seeking father and the fiancée of one of the missing ended their lives.

Trump stated that the US is at war with the biggest supporter of terrorism. These remarks were made in the audio version of the program 24 with Fardad Farahzad. The topic is related to war and terrorism.

Britain has passed a new law to impose tougher sanctions against the Islamic Republic. These sanctions send a message to both the Islamic Republic and the United States, indicating London's alignment with the US economic ostracism policy. Britain has stated its full readiness to participate in the economic campaign against the Islamic Republic.

Donya-e-Eqtesad newspaper reported that Iran's foreign trade crisis has spread from the sea to land borders and financial routes. Media reported the accumulation of 17,000 containers at Karachi port and the stoppage of thousands of trucks at Pakistan's borders. This issue was discussed in an interview with Mahtab Gholizadeh.

Gideon Sa'ar, Israel's Foreign Minister, announced the closure of the British consulate in East Jerusalem in response to Britain's sanctions against Israeli settlements. Entry of 10 British officials and citizens to Israel will also be banned. Sa'ar described Britain's sanctions as interference in Israel's upcoming elections.

The mother of Siavash Mahmoudi, a protester killed in the "Woman, Life, Freedom" uprising, joined the "One Candle, One Name, One Memory" campaign. She lit a candle for her son and said he was a cry for freedom and liberty.

A grandmother who supports Esteghlal said she offered a bribe to her grandchildren who support Persepolis to change their team. Her grandchildren replied that their blood is red and they will not change their team. This interview was conducted by Football 360.

South Korea's Ministry of Defense has sent a team to assess the security situation in the Strait of Hormuz. No decision has been made yet about deploying military forces to the area. This move follows the reduction of joint military exercises between the US and South Korea.

Farshid Esmaeili broke the door of the referees' room after the match between Zob Ahan and Persepolis in protest against the refereeing. Zob Ahan players believed there was a suspicious penalty, but the referee ended the game without reviewing the scene. The match ended with a 2-0 victory for Persepolis.

A shopkeeper in Rasht market reported power outages and rainwater entering his shop. He also complained about the business downturn. He attributed this situation to the actions of the Islamic Republic.

A video shows that on September 6, military forces on motorcycles were present in the streets of Tabriz. This video was received by Iran International. The presence of military forces on this date has been documented.

The Russian Foreign Minister announced that Russia and Saudi Arabia will continue their close cooperation and coordination within the OPEC+ framework to stabilize the global oil market. This announcement was made at a joint press conference in Moscow. More details are available in an interview with an Iran International reporter.

Between 30 to 40 percent of parents who divorce in Iran have at least one child. Approximately 200,000 divorces are registered annually, leading to children being involved in custody disputes. These children are caught between their parents' homes, police stations, and courts.

Narges Heydari, a political prisoner from Izeh, was sentenced to five years in prison and one year of additional punishment due to her sports activities without mandatory hijab. She is held in Sepidar Prison in Ahvaz and was arrested on January 18, 2026. Her brother was also arrested earlier.

Houthis released a video showing an attack on Saudi trucks near Al-Wadiah on the Yemen-Saudi border. The trucks were burning and had entered from Saudi Arabia. Houthis stated that these trucks were targeted in the attack.

The Islamic Republic's delegation stated at the IAEA Board of Governors meeting that the agency is responsible for illegal attacks on peaceful nuclear facilities under inspection. The delegation highlighted breaches of confidentiality and misuse of sensitive information. They also questioned how member states can trust the agency's performance if it does not adequately address nuclear security consequences.

An online taxi driver criticized the increase in gasoline prices in a video. He said that with the current quota and price of gasoline, working is not profitable. He also warned that everything is going to become more expensive.
The sixth week of the Persian Gulf Pro League ended with four matches. Persepolis defeated Zob Ahan 2-0 in an important match. This victory moved Persepolis up to second place in the standings.

Rasoul Karbakandi criticized Tractor Club's support of Khodadad Azizi's insulting behavior in the Tractor vs Gol Gohar match case. He stated that Iranian football has strayed from ethical paths and current sanctions lack deterrent effect. Karbakandi called for decisive action from authorities without any considerations.

Faisal bin Farhan, Saudi Arabia's foreign minister, stated that the country will use all available tools to protect its interests. He accused the Houthis of prioritizing their own interests over those of the Yemeni people and resorting to violence in difficult situations. The foreign minister also said that the diplomatic path to confront the Houthis remains open.

Abdolkareem Hashemi Nakhl Ebrahimi, a member of parliament, stated that the people of the region and the guardians of the Strait of Hormuz are ready to confront the enemy using small boats. He added that if the US does not accept the Islamic Republic's conditions, they must powerfully attack the enemy's naval fleet and break the naval blockade. The goal is to expel the enemy from the region.

Families and relatives of those who died in the December protests have launched a campaign called "One Candle, One Name, One Memory." The campaign involves lighting candles and remembering the names and memories of the deceased to keep their memory alive. More details were provided by Farnoush Faraji, a member of the Iran International editorial team.

A citizen in a video commented on inflation in Iran, saying that a day's wage is now equivalent to the price of a sandwich. He pointed to the decline in wage value. This statement was sent to Iran International.

The UK government issued a new law on September 7 to intensify sanctions against the Islamic Republic. The law expands trade restrictions and the authority to target ships. It also bans Iranian planes from landing in the UK except in exempted cases.

A citizen protested the increase in gasoline prices in a video. He said that Pezeshkian had stated that permission would be obtained from the people for the price hike, but no such permission was taken. He also mentioned that the price of motor oil has increased by 50 percent.

Israel hosted the first international physical artificial intelligence conference in Tel Aviv. The conference was held in cooperation with the National AI Headquarters at the Israeli Prime Minister's Office. It focused on the connection between artificial intelligence, robotics, and autonomous systems.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated that the Islamic Republic has always opposed war and considers preserving people's interests and regional security by avoiding arson. He added that the Islamic Republic has resisted aggression and will continue this resistance until the aggressors fully regret it.

Arash Azarmi from Iran International stated that the third gasoline rate has doubled and each liter is sold for 10,000 tomans with fuel cards. He considers fuel pricing policies, currency devaluation, the worn-out car crisis, and automaker monopolies as factors worsening the crisis. According to Azarmi, the cost of these inefficient policies is ultimately borne by the people.

Tractor club filed a complaint against Persepolis for insulting and racist chants against their manager Khodadad Azizi and threats to their players. These incidents occurred during the Persepolis and Zob Ahan match. The football federation's disciplinary committee also punished Azizi and Omid Alishah with suspensions and fines.

Jose Mourinho begins his second coaching period at Real Madrid with a Champions League match against Inter Milan. Real Madrid seeks victory after a recent loss in La Liga. Inter, boosted by a recent comeback win against Napoli, heads to Santiago Bernabeu with high morale.

Mohammad Taghi Naqdali, representative of Khomeini Shahr, said the government has retreated on the issue of hijab and compromised religious principles. He also mentioned the government's bypassing of the Supreme Council of Cyberspace and failure to enforce the hijab law. Naqdali stated that the counter-infiltration plan and hijab are revolutionary slogans that will be pursued.

Citizens have reacted to the increase in gasoline price to 10,000 tomans, seeing it as a cause for rising prices of bread, fares, and other goods. They believe this increase has made life harder and increased economic pressure. They also demand wages to be raised proportionally to the price hikes.

A citizen reported on the evening of Tuesday, September 6, that some fuel stations were closed and did not allow cars to refuel. This happened ahead of the gasoline price increase. The related video was sent to Iran International.

A group of nurses in Kermanshah gathered on Tuesday, 17 Shahrivar, to protest their living conditions. They chanted that they have no salaries and the police are brought in. The protest was held due to the financial problems of the nurses.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh warned about currency resource limitations and difficulties in importing gasoline. He mentioned the possibility of the government transferring the financial burden of deficits to the people. He also said the consequences of fuel price increases may appear later in various economic and livelihood sectors.

The Saudi Foreign Ministry announced that the east-west oil pipeline was attacked by drones launched from Iraq. Saudi Arabia has decided not to take retaliatory action at this stage. The country reserves the right to take all necessary measures to protect its security.

Mohsen Modir Shanechi said the US primarily uses economic and financial tools to besiege the Islamic Republic and employs military power if necessary. He identified inflation as a key indicator of the Islamic Republic's resilience. Rising dollar and essential goods prices indicate increasing pressure on Iran's economy.

Omid Memarian stated that despite the growing Muslim population in the US, memories of the 9/11 attacks and wars with extremist groups have increased negative views of Islam. He added that generalizing extremist actions to all Muslims has played a significant role in this perception. This issue has intensified over the past 25 years.

The French army announced that the Aspides mission to protect ships in the Bab al-Mandab Strait continues. The Houthi military spokesperson stated that navigation is safe for all ships except Saudi vessels. These statements were made amid regional tensions.

Erfan from Bandar Abbas stated that southern Iran is now like southern Lebanon. He mentioned that army units are also stationed in mosques. This report was broadcast in a program on Iran International TV.

Mohammad Taghavi commented on Esteghlal's victory over Paykan in the seventh week of the Premier League, saying Esteghlal did not perform well but had to win the match. He added that Esteghlal's defense line is disorganized and will face problems in Asian matches.

Shahrzad Zamiri, a political prisoner and former police colonel, was summoned again to the military prosecutor's office after being released on bail. She was arrested following the December protests and held in solitary confinement for about two months. Her charges are related to assisting protesters.

The CENTCOM commander has traveled to Saudi Arabia for urgent talks. Concerns have increased about the opening of a new front in the battle with the Houthis. American forces are monitoring the Islamic Republic's activities supporting Houthi attacks.

The crew of the American aircraft carrier USS George Washington is preparing for battle with the Islamic Republic. This ship has been dispatched to replace the USS Abraham Lincoln. Both carriers have been deployed to strengthen the US naval blockade in the Middle East.

Mohammad Qaedi said the Islamic Republic's goal in escalating tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab is to pressure the global economy, especially the US economy. He added that the US prefers to focus on the Strait of Hormuz rather than directly engaging in battle with the Houthis. The US has delegated the main role in confronting the Houthis to Saudi Arabia.

Mehdi Moslehi stated that the reduction in Iran's oil loading does not mean definite exports, and the US naval blockade has created serious obstacles. He said the global oil market is not facing a physical shortage, and price increases are due to transportation and insurance risks. Saudi Arabia and other regional producers continue their exports.

New Delhi will host the 18th BRICS summit starting September 12. Leaders of emerging economic powers will discuss Middle East crises, the Ukraine war, and reforms in the global financial system during the two-day meeting. Multilateral trade development is also on the agenda.
On the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks, a ceremony was held at the 9/11 memorial in Los Angeles. The victims of the attacks and fallen first responders were commemorated.

The Iraqi Prime Minister's office announced the dismissal of a military commander after investigations into drone attacks on Saudi Arabia. The investigation confirmed that the drones took off from Iraqi territory. The Prime Minister also ordered the formation of a committee to review the operations command in Maysan province.

Kylian Mbappé criticized memes comparing him to dictators, calling such comparisons inaccurate. He understands the humorous aspect of these memes but believes they downplay serious issues. Mbappé expressed this in an interview with France Football.

Alireza Sepahi, one of the December protesters, has been transferred from the general ward to solitary confinement in Dastgerd prison in Isfahan. There is a possibility that his death sentence will be carried out in the coming days. Mahmoudian stated that Sepahi and other defendants were tortured during detention and their confessions were extracted under pressure.

Yechiel Leiter, Israel's ambassador to the US, stated that Israel will not accept anything less than the collapse of the Islamic Republic. He added that victory over the Islamic Republic requires the collapse of the regime, and the timing of this collapse is uncertain. Leiter also emphasized that Iran's political future must be determined by the Iranian people.

The Trump administration provides significant intelligence to Saudi Arabia but currently has no plans for direct military attacks against the Houthis. This stance may change if threats to shipping in the Red Sea increase significantly. Mohammed bin Salman has requested direct US military intervention.

The office of Prince Reza Pahlavi warned about the possible execution of Alireza Sepahi, a December protester, after his transfer to solitary confinement. The office stated that the Islamic Republic repeatedly uses this process to reduce public sensitivity to the risk of execution. They called for increased attention to the fate of political prisoners.

The Wall Street Journal reported that Iran obtained high-resolution satellite images from Chinese entities before the deadly missile attack on a base in Jordan. China has denied this. The attack killed three American soldiers and wounded four others, and Iran also targeted manned and unmanned aircraft at the base.

Kayhan newspaper, in response to the IAEA Board of Governors resolution, called for Iran to leave the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) and stop inspectors' access to nuclear facilities. The newspaper described the Western-backed resolution as political and legally baseless, stating that Iran's continued membership in the NPT is unjustified without security guarantees for nuclear sites. Kayhan also urged the government to halt safeguard cooperation until security assurances are received.

HalVash website reported that a severe clash between military and security forces and unknown armed individuals began around 4 AM on Saturday, September 11th, in the Bakhshan area of Saravan county. The conflict lasted more than three hours, and local sources reported hearing at least 14 explosions and rapid gunfire. HalVash also reported that several reconnaissance drones were seen over the area and ambulance sirens were heard in the vicinity of the clashes.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated that the Strait of Hormuz will be reopened if the US stops its blockade and attacks on Iran. He emphasized that the US cannot force the Islamic Republic to surrender through continued pressure. He also mentioned the agreement between Iran and Oman and the upcoming meeting of Arab foreign ministers in Muscat.

The deputy security official of Khuzestan province announced that the Shalamcheh and Chazabeh borders have been closed from early Saturday until further notice, with no movement of goods or passengers. This action was taken by Iraq following a drone attack on the Saudi oil pipeline. Iraqi forces have launched a wide operation to identify the perpetrators of the attack.

Hossein Aghaei stated that the Islamic Republic has opened two fronts in the region by the Houthis' advance in the Bab al-Mandab Strait. The Houthis aim to bring Saudi Arabia to the negotiating table and gain concessions. Additionally, the Islamic Republic is escalating tensions to pressure Saudi Arabia to encourage Washington to negotiate.

Ahmad Alavi, an economist, stated that sanctions play an important role in spreading corruption, but corruption is structural. He added that in conditions of reduced foreign exchange income, the government prioritizes repression. The budget for public welfare, education, social security, and healthcare decreases.

The body of Javad Mojabi, poet and writer, was buried in Emamzadeh Taher in Karaj. He passed away at the age of 87 in Tehran. Mojabi was an influential figure in contemporary Iranian literature and culture.

Ily Mahfouz, head of the Lebanese Change Movement, said Lebanon should have cut ties with the Islamic Republic from the start and banned Hezbollah's activities. He called for the expulsion of the Iranian ambassador and prosecution of Hezbollah leaders. He also emphasized that weapons and sovereignty should be solely under the Lebanese government's control.

Nazli Sedghi stated that Alireza Sepahi has been transferred to solitary confinement and there is a possibility of his execution. She pointed out serious legal issues in the case, including Sepahi's absence at the scene of the incident and confessions made under torture. It was also mentioned that the parallel branch likely issued a rejection of the retrial without holding a session.

Kayhan newspaper criticized Majid Ansari, deputy of Masoud Pezeshkian, for stating that the hijab law is unenforceable. Kayhan described these remarks as passive and shirking responsibility. The newspaper urged the government's legal deputy to provide legal solutions.

The Law School Admission Council (LSAC) in the US has stopped providing some services to Iranian users due to changes in US sanctions regulations. This restriction was imposed after the US Treasury suspended a license that allowed educational services to Iranians indefinitely. Services will resume for those who present exemption documents.

Majid Mousavi, commander of the IRGC Aerospace Force, stated that the US has built a drone similar to the Shahed 136 called "Lucas" and integrated it into its combat organization. He also mentioned that various Shahed-class drones are used by the IRGC for combat and reconnaissance missions. The drone forces have played an important role in monitoring areas and conducting cross-border missions.

The Iraqi Dijlah network reported that flights from Iran and to Iran have been canceled until further notice. The Shalamcheh and Chazabeh border crossings have also been closed, stopping the movement of goods and passengers. The Esteghlal football team may travel via a flight to Baghdad and then to Basra.

Anthropic company announced that Iranian government-related entities have used Claude AI for monitoring citizens and opponents. The company blocked 16 accounts linked to two security and paramilitary units. Additionally, three propaganda operations using AI-generated fake personas and independent-appearing content were identified and related accounts were blocked.

The sister of Erfan Kiani, a protester killed in December 2025, joined the "One Candle, One Name, One Memory" campaign. She visited the tomb of her brother and other martyrs of the National Iranian Revolution. She said they light a candle so their names are not forgotten in the darkness.

The identities of four more Sunni citizens arrested in Ahvaz, including Mostafa Cheldavi, Ali Cheldavi, Ebrahim Hamdani, and Hadi Beit Sheikh Ahmad, have been confirmed. These individuals were arrested by security forces on Thursday, September 9, 2026, in the village of Oboudeh, Ahvaz. Previously, the identities of five other citizens had also been confirmed.

Abbas Aliabadi, the Minister of Energy, mentioned the possibility of heavy rainfall and said the country needs water. He emphasized the need to be prepared for upcoming conditions and not to be caught off guard. He also noted that it might not be possible to prevent all damages.

Mohammadreza Mohseni-Thani stated that Iran no longer considers itself bound by the NPT and that increasing uranium enrichment levels is possible. He said the Islamic Republic has no limits on uranium enrichment to any level it deems necessary. He also mentioned that the presence of IAEA inspectors in Iran is ruled out.

Family members and close friends commemorated Mehrab Golestani's birthday at his gravesite. Mehrab Golestani was a 17-year-old teenager who was shot by government agents in Isfahan on the evening of January 9 and died. He was born in Kerman and was a student at a gifted school in Isfahan.

District 12 of Tehran has the largest area of worn-out texture with about 586 hectares. Districts 11 and 10 follow with 371 and 342 hectares respectively. Additionally, about 3,768 hectares of unstable texture exist in Tehran, mostly located in several specified districts.

Mehdi Rouzbehani has been held in Isfahan's Dastgerd prison since March 18, 2026, without his trial being held. He faces charges including insulting the leadership and propaganda against the regime. His previous lawyer withdrew due to security threats.

Iran's national volleyball team defeated Australia 3-1 in the Asian Championship semifinals, advancing to the final. The win also secured their ninth qualification for the 2027 World Cup. Iran will face the winner of the Japan-South Korea match in the final.

Ebrahim Azizi, head of the National Security Commission, stated that resistance groups will not be disarmed and the US will fail in this effort. He added that the Islamic Republic has expanded its defensive borders. Azizi mentioned significant achievements in this conflict.

Masoud Pezeshkian, head of the Islamic Republic government, met with Droupadi Murmu, President of India, in New Delhi on Saturday, September 12. He traveled to India to attend the BRICS summit. Narendra Modi, India's Prime Minister, also met with Pezeshkian on Friday and emphasized the importance of maintaining freedom of navigation.

Ali Shirazi stated that the decision about continuing the war and the Strait of Hormuz is not in Masoud Pezeshkian's hands, but the IRGC is responsible. He added that the IRGC has assigned an international role to Pezeshkian to portray the Islamic Republic as a victim.

Ghasem Ravanbakhsh, representative of Qom in the parliament, stated that the Islamic Republic is prepared to confront the US naval blockade. He added that this blockade can be countered with military and defensive measures. The goal is to maintain the routes of Iranian ships.

Donald Trump, during his trip to Ireland, said that everything will go well regarding the Iran war. He made this statement in response to a question about helping ships pass through the Strait of Hormuz. These remarks came amid new concerns from Saudi Arabia.

The head of Iran's Food and Drug Organization stated that the supply of medicine, medical equipment, and infant formula in the country is severely affected by increasing health challenges. Mohsen Mahimini reports on citizens' messages regarding the crisis of medicine and health items.

A ceremony for the birthday of Mohammad Farhadi, a protester killed in December 2025, was held at his grave in Qarchak. Women from his family cried out in mourning during the event. A video of the ceremony has been shared on social media.

Ahmad Vahidi, commander of the IRGC, stated that the Israeli army would collapse quickly without US support. He added that Iran's military power exceeds enemy expectations and accused Trump of resorting to lies for achievements. Vahidi also emphasized that US political officials deceive the public to cover up failures.

Bank Sepah issued a directive warning contract employees to pursue their labor protests only through authorized channels. The directive, dated September 8, 2026, states that unprofessional behavior will lead to disciplinary action. This comes amid worsening economic crisis and protests by contract employees in state banks.

US President Donald Trump, in response to reporters' questions about whether the Islamic Republic was responsible for the attack on the Saudi East-West pipeline, said: 'I think so. It was probably them.'

There is heavy congestion at the Bazargan border, causing long waits for Iranian travelers entering Turkey. Iranian officials have stated that the border is open. The main issue is increased traffic and limited capacity on the Turkish side.

The Quds Headquarters of the IRGC Ground Forces announced that three of their members were killed in a military clash with armed individuals in Saravan. Additionally, four unknown armed individuals were killed in the clash. This incident occurred before noon on Saturday.

The director of the Compensation Fund for Bodily Injuries stated that over 20,000 people die annually in traffic accidents. Around 400,000 people are injured, with 70,000 to 80,000 suffering amputations or disabilities. Additionally, about 90% of gasoline motorcycles are worn out, and over 50% of motorcycle accidents result in death.

A citizen reported in a video to Iran International that a well-known dairy producer is underdelivering cheese despite price increases. This issue has raised concerns about the quality and quantity of dairy products.

Masoud Pezeshkian emphasized the role of BRICS in resolving the Palestine issue at the BRICS summit in India. He announced the Islamic Republic's support for strengthening political coordination and developing economic and scientific cooperation within BRICS. He also highlighted the priority of combating unilateral sanctions and respecting countries' territories.

The German Federal Prosecutor has accused seven Hamas members of attempting to procure weapons and ammunition for terrorist operations in Europe. These weapons were intended for attacks against Israeli and Jewish targets in Germany and other European countries. The trial reveals new aspects of Hamas's network activities in Europe.

Taraneh and Romina Rahimi, two sisters arrested during the protests of January 2026, are held in Dolatabad prison in Isfahan. Taraneh Rahimi has been sentenced to death and 11 years in prison, and Romina Rahimi to 36 years in prison. Their charges include moharebeh and assisting moharebeh, and their confessions were obtained under pressure and torture.

Videos published on social media show congestion at the Bazargan border exit. Some reports attribute the disruption to capacity limitations on the Turkish side. This has caused traffic disruptions at this border crossing.

A 13-year-old teenager talks about his family's economic problems and the high costs of school supplies and tuition. He calls for an end to the war and reopening schools without financial worries. Families are facing severe economic pressure to afford education expenses.

The Wrestling Federation confirmed its exemption from obtaining technical and financial qualification certificates to enter the mining sector. The federation considers the right to engage in economic and mining activities based on its statute. It was also stated that, unlike the usual procedure, it can enter the process of registering exploration areas without having the qualification certificates.

The Wrestling Federation of the Islamic Republic stated that its economic and mining activities are conducted according to its statutes and the law. This response was made regarding controversies about exemption from obtaining technical and financial qualification certificates. The statement was part of an interview with sports journalist Mehdi Rostampour.

Mohammad Sadegh Motamedian, the governor of Tehran, called for the return of schools that have been taken over by other organizations. He emphasized that these educational spaces must be returned to the Ministry of Education before the start of the school year. The governor did not specify which organizations are involved.

The Iranian national basketball team lost 59-53 to Qatar in their first game at the Nagoya Asian Games. The first quarter ended tied at 10-10, and Qatar led 31-21 at halftime. Iran will next face Taiwan and Jordan in the group stage.

Lamine Yamal became the youngest captain in Barcelona's history at 19 years and 58 days old. He received the captain's armband from Rafinha during the match against Feyenoord and scored six minutes later. The previous record was held by Bojan Krkic, who became captain at 20 years and 56 days old.

Roghayeh Rezaei reported an increase in the prices of menstrual hygiene products. She stated that the Islamic Republic imposes restrictions on women's bodies alongside pro-natalist policies. Additionally, necessary support for women's healthcare is not provided.

The "Jan Faday Iran" exercise will be held on September 17 with the participation of Basij forces, the Revolutionary Guards, and police. The commander of Tehran's Revolutionary Guards stated that this exercise demonstrates the readiness and determination of the Iranian nation. Its purpose is declared to confront the enemies.

The heads of parliaments of the G7 countries announced at the end of their meeting in Paris that the Islamic Republic must never acquire nuclear weapons. This statement was made at the recent G7 meeting. The report was provided by Sajedeh Sharifi from Iran International.

Hossein Ali Hajideligani, a member of parliament, called for conducting necessary tests for nuclear weapons. He stated that the reason is the Islamic Republic's need for nuclear deterrence power. A three-urgency plan to withdraw Iran from the NPT treaty has also been prepared.

Marzieh Hosseini, a reporter for Iran International, has reported on Donald Trump's speech at the Republican gathering. She mentioned the possibility of another US attack on the Kooh Kalang facilities. She also examined the connection between the war with the Islamic Republic and the US midterm elections.

Sahar Khodayari, an Esteghlal fan, self-immolated in protest against a six-month prison sentence for attempting to enter Azadi Stadium and died on September 9, 2019. She had been accused of various charges including public indecency. Her death received widespread international attention.

Shahram Kholdi referred to Donald Trump's statements about the attack on the Kuh-e-Kalang facility and said that if the attack does not lead to the complete destruction of the facility, the Islamic Republic will move towards militarizing its nuclear program.

Shayan Samiei said Trump has left the door open for negotiations with the Islamic Republic but considers the previous agreement ended. He added that Trump sends a message to the Iranian people that they are separate from the government.

Donald Trump warned the Islamic Republic about activities at Kuh-e Kalanq Gezla and said Iran should not have nuclear weapons. He emphasized that Iran cannot have nuclear weapons and criticized past efforts to negotiate with Iran. Trump also mentioned the possibility of targeting these facilities.

Donald Trump stated that the decision to attack Iran's nuclear facilities was made after receiving reports about Tehran's proximity to nuclear weapons. He said some officials wanted to delay the attack, but he opposed it. Trump also discussed the bomber operation and the possibility of attacking Kuh-e Kolang Gazla.

Donald Trump said at a Republican gathering in Dallas that the war with the Islamic Republic will end shortly after the November 3 midterm elections. He added that Tehran wants a deal with the Democrats.

Reuters, citing a CBS reporter, reported that several US military aircraft were damaged in nighttime attacks on the Al-Salti airbase in Jordan. An A-10 Thunderbolt lost one of its wings, and about eight F-15s sustained minor damage but returned to service. The Islamic Republic announced that it had targeted the base with ballistic missiles.

The Saudi-led coalition announced that the Houthis targeted the cities of Khamis Mushait, Abha, and Jazan with ballistic missiles and drones on Wednesday, September 8. The coalition spokesperson stated that their response to these attacks will be within the framework of the right to self-defense. Additionally, Saudi Arabia has asked Iran through Pakistan to influence the Houthis to stop the attacks, but Tehran said it does not control the Houthis.

The Wall Street Journal, quoting American officials, reported that senior White House advisors have discussed with President Donald Trump the possibility of the war with the Islamic Republic continuing until the end of his presidency and even beyond January 2029. According to the report, JD Vance, the US Vice President, Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, and other officials discussed the possibility of Tehran continuing its resistance against military siege and pressures. This assessment differs from Trump's public statements, where he said the war would end "immediately" after the November midterm elections.

The Islamic Republic used missiles equipped with electro-optical guidance systems for the first time in attacks on US warships on Wednesday, September 8. CENTCOM confirmed the missile attacks but stated that no ships were hit. The Revolutionary Guards claimed to have targeted two American vessels and several tankers and ships.

The Transitional Justice Committee, chaired by Shirin Ebadi, warned the commanders and executors of protesters' executions that each of them will be held accountable. The committee stated that no leniency will be shown and all legal tools will be used for prosecution and punishment. It also emphasized that each execution increases criminal responsibility and these crimes will not be forgotten.

The Center for Strategic and International Studies reported that satellite images show increased construction activities in the underground complex of Kuh-e Kalang Gazla near the Natanz nuclear facility in 2026. Activities have shifted from excavation to internal construction and tunnel entrance reinforcement. The center neither confirmed nor denied claims of centrifuge transfers to this complex.

Erfan Haj Bonyan Dehaghani, detained in connection with the December 1404 protests in Isfahan, was sentenced to one year in prison. He was also sentenced to 10 years in prison for non-political charges. The verdict was issued on August 11 by the Revolutionary Court of Isfahan.

Arash Azarmi from Iran International stated that the factors causing turmoil in the currency market have not improved but worsened. Regional conflicts and decreased foreign exchange income and exports are reasons for this situation. The Central Bank either does not have or does not use a policy of injecting currency into the market.

Hadad Adel stated that the Islamic Republic has failed regarding women's dress code. He said policies that ignore women's right to choose have caused this failure. He also emphasized that people have not been influenced by enemy infiltration but have moved beyond the government's policies.

Hadad Adel said that the Islamic Republic's work on women's dress has become more difficult and that the enemy promotes a Western lifestyle. He mentioned the failure of policies that do not recognize women as having the right to choose. This topic is discussed in a program hosted by Kambiz Hosseini.

The Iranian Transitional Justice Committee warned the perpetrators and commanders of protester executions that these crimes will be pursued without leniency. Afshin Elyan emphasized the need to document executions and human rights violations, stating those involved will face legal responsibility. He urged citizens to securely keep documents related to executions for use in transitional justice and international legal proceedings.

Zahra Naqsineh, a lawyer and member of the East Azerbaijan Bar Association, was arrested on Wednesday, 18 Shahrivar, at Branch 15 of the Tabriz Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor's Office. The arrest occurred after her presence at the judicial authority. Harana News Agency reported this news.

Arash Aramesh, a lawyer and security expert, said the Trump administration has not yet made a final decision on its ultimate strategy towards the Islamic Republic. He added that the US is currently between three options: escalating the war, continuing the status quo, or moving towards a deal, and it is not yet clear which path it will choose. He also said the US has the military capability to conduct limited ground operations, including on some strategic Iranian islands, but the decision depends more on political will than military factors.

Reuters reported that Iran has obtained a US Navy underwater drone. The drone, an older Dive-LD model, was found by Iranian forces after a technical failure. Iran may reverse-engineer parts of the drone, but this is unlikely to provide a decisive military advantage for Tehran.

Chris Wright, the US Energy Secretary, announced that more contracts with oil companies in Venezuela will be announced soon. He previously said these contracts would more than double Venezuela's oil production. Increased investment in Venezuela's energy sector could significantly boost oil production capacity.

Hossein Mohebbi, spokesperson for the IRGC, dismissed Benjamin Netanyahu's threats and considered Israel too small to carry out threats against Iran. Netanyahu had stated that Israel is ready to act against Iran if necessary. He also said that they must finish what they started with the Islamic Republic.

The defense company Covenant, supported by Peter Thiel, has started producing long-range, low-cost cruise missiles. The company designed the 'Anthem' missile with heavy payload capacity and has conducted about 200 test flights. Covenant has received orders worth $150 million, with deliveries starting in 2027.

Railway workers protested in front of the Ministry of Roads and Urban Development in Tehran. They protested against repression and poor living conditions, chanting slogans against the minister. They threatened to strike if their problems were not resolved.

A program with Kambiz Hosseini about unprecedented sanctions on Iranian aviation has been released. The program discusses the possibility of all flights being canceled. The main topic is the sanctions and their impact on Iran's flights.

Palmer Luckey, founder of Anduril, stated that the Dive-DL drone is designed so that losing it in operations does not create a security problem. The drone is made for extremely dangerous environments and its loss is acceptable. He added that the device provided significant operational value for months before falling into enemy hands.

Several explosions were heard in the coastal areas of Qeshm, Sirik, and Minab in the early hours of Thursday, September 19. The Hormozgan governorate stated that the sounds came from the sea, and no reports about the cause or damage have been released yet. The explosions were strong enough to shake buildings and windows.

Esmaeil Baqaei, spokesperson for Iran's Foreign Ministry, denied Marco Rubio's claims that the Houthis are proxies of Iran, stating that the Houthis are an independent actor who take their own decisions. This response came after Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia that injured at least 73 people. It was also reported that Saudi Arabia sent a message through Pakistan asking Iran to intervene to stop the Houthi attacks.

Rouhollah Najabat stated that the Islamic Republic will accelerate the technical development of its nuclear program in response to the IAEA Board of Governors resolution. He emphasized that Iran will not give any concessions and will respond more firmly. Najabat also described the resolution as political and held Western countries responsible for any potential tensions.

The Yemeni Armed Forces Media Center released a video showing clashes between Saudi-backed government forces and Houthi forces near Al Hazm. These clashes have intensified in recent months, raising concerns about a return to a broader war. Yemeni government forces have launched a multi-front attack to reclaim areas controlled by the Houthis.

The Yemeni Armed Forces Media Center released a video showing clashes between Saudi-backed government forces and Houthi forces. The exact time and location of the video recording have not been confirmed. Clashes have intensified recently, and Yemeni government forces have launched a multi-front attack on Houthi-controlled areas.

Alireza Salimi stated that leaving the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) could be one of Iran's options to respond to the IAEA Board of Governors resolution. He described the resolution as political and hostile and said Iran has not benefited from the treaty's rights. Salimi predicted that actions related to the resolution would face a veto due to Russia and China's membership in the Security Council.

Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, said that the Islamic Republic has not received assistance to change the war conditions. He added that the Islamic Republic attacks US Navy ships but has lost five of its oil tankers in response. Rubio emphasized that the US will continue to economically suffocate the Islamic Republic.

The mother of Setareh Rafiei lit a candle in the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory" in memory of her daughter. Setareh Rafiei, 19 years old, was killed on January 9, 2026, in Narmak, Tehran. Her mother stated that she neither forgives nor forgets.

The head of the Iranian Gastrointestinal Endoscopy Association warned about a 59% increase in liver cancer over the past 10 years. Shahram Kordasti attributed this rise to poor nutrition, fatty liver, and weak prevention programs. He emphasized the importance of prevention and the challenges in accessing medical services.

Al Nassr football team defeated Abha 2-1 in the sixth week of the Saudi Professional League. Cristiano Ronaldo scored the first goal in the 22nd minute, bringing his career goal tally to 979. With this win, Al Nassr achieved their fifth victory and tied in points with Al Hilal and Al Qadsiah.

A citizen installed a street sign named Mahsa Amini Street in eastern Seyyed Ghotb Street, Piranshahr, on the eve of the anniversary of Mahsa Zeina Amini's death. This act is shown in a video received by Iran International.

Farzin Nadimi stated that conventional bombs may not be sufficient to completely destroy the underground facilities of Kuh-e Kalang-Gazla. The Pentagon is considering developing more advanced penetrator weapons and new operational scenarios. Additionally, locations near the Strait of Hormuz hold greater military significance than Khark Island.

Meir Javdanfar said there are signs of increasing disagreement between Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu. Their relations remain good, but Trump's stance on the upcoming Israeli elections is important. Among Trump's advisors, there is also disagreement on how to deal with Netanyahu.

A citizen stated in a video that last year he started a business by selling his gold but has not recovered his initial capital until now. He shared this issue on social media. This complaint points to financial problems in the business.

Pakistan has conveyed Saudi Arabia's message to Tehran, asking Iran to use its influence to stop Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. Tehran responded that it does not control the Houthis. Sources also said that last week Tehran asked the Houthis to attack Saudi Arabia and promised financial and military support.

Sardar Azmoun has been re-invited to the Iranian national football team after recent controversies and government criticisms. He is expected to participate in the upcoming FIFA international window and preparations for the Asian Cup. This return comes after Azmoun distanced himself from the national team and had his assets seized.

A video from the evening of September 8 shows that a government gathering in one of the squares in Qom was sparse. The seats at this gathering were mostly empty. This video was received by Iran International.

Donald Trump stated that the war with Iran will end immediately after the 2026 US elections. He said he is no longer seeking an agreement with the Islamic Republic and that negotiations might occur but are not the current focus. Trump also mentioned working on matters beyond the nuclear deal, involving new issues.

A citizen says they have to buy various medicines every month but the prices have become very expensive. They are worried they might not be able to afford their medicines anymore. They also attribute the rise in medicine prices to the increase in gasoline prices.

Ismail Baqaei, the Foreign Ministry spokesperson, said that referring Iran's nuclear case to the UN Security Council is irrelevant because Iran has not violated any commitments. He attributed the issues raised in the Board of Governors resolution to attacks by the US and Israel. Baqaei described Japan and Saudi Arabia's positive vote on the resolution as ineffective.

Mohammed bin Zayed, the UAE president, warned Netanyahu about Yahya Sinwar's plan to attack Israel one week before October 7. Netanyahu denied the warning and said no such call took place. UAE officials neither confirmed nor denied the report.

An informed source told Iran International that the health and humanitarian situation in Qom Central Prison is dire. Most prisoners have contracted influenza and COVID-19. The prison environment is heavily contaminated and the prisoners' daily food rations are insufficient.

A US official told NewsNation that American forces are not conducting any attacks near Jask, following reports of an explosion sound. The Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting had reported hearing an explosion from the direction of the Strait of Hormuz in Jask on Wednesday evening.

Alireza Ardoubadi resigned from the Persepolis club board. Hossein Saberi was introduced as the new member and chairman of the board. Ardoubadi left Persepolis due to his candidacy for the Bank Shahr board.

A video has been released showing a young woman singing a local song at the grave of Omid Sarlak. She pays respect in front of his picture installed at the grave. Omid Sarlak, a 27-year-old athlete from Aligudarz, was suspiciously killed in November 2025.

Eight months after the killing of protesters in January 2026, images of body bags that families search through to find their loved ones remain in the collective memory of Iranians. These bags have become a symbol of death and repression in recent protests. Previously, such images were mostly seen in cinema and natural disasters.

Benjamin Netanyahu stated that Israel will not allow any terrorist army to be stationed on its borders. He called the Islamic Republic a terrorist regime and said Israel's main goal is to defeat the Iranian government. Netanyahu also mentioned Israel's unprecedented control over the region.

The US Central Command announced that American forces destroyed five Iranian oil tankers. CENTCOM denied the IRGC's claim of targeting two American warships. The Saudi foreign minister warned about the consequences of Houthi attacks.

An electronics specialist and industrial board repair technician stated that he has not found work for several years and his life situation is disrupted. This was reported in a video to Iran International. He is experiencing difficult circumstances.

Fars news agency reported hearing an explosion sound on Wednesday evening in Jask. The sound was heard from the sea in the southern areas of Jask county. The source of this news is Fars, affiliated with the Revolutionary Guards.

The Israeli Prime Minister said Israel will not allow any terrorist army to be stationed on its borders during a visit to the army positions on Mount Hermon. He called the Islamic Republic a terrorist regime and stated that Israel's main goal is to defeat the Iranian government. Netanyahu added that they are close to achieving this goal.

Saeed Javanmard, a former army officer, has been sentenced to a total of eight years in prison in two judicial cases. He was expelled from the army and sentenced to three years in prison after participating in the 1401 protests. In a new case, he was sentenced to five years for charges including cooperation with hostile states and disrupting order.

Reza Najafi stated that with the end of the war, verification activities by the agency in Iran will be possible. He said the comprehensive safeguards agreement does not have specific regulations for wartime conditions. He also emphasized that military attacks by the US and Israel have affected the implementation of safeguards in Iran.

The United States has sanctioned 27 companies and entities related to Iranian aviation and suspended three general licenses in this sector. The stated goal of these sanctions is to increase pressure on the Islamic Republic. This decision may affect travel for medical treatment, education, work, and family visits.

Ali Tajernia, acting CEO of Esteghlal club, stated that the club is requesting the championship trophy for the unfinished season. He emphasized that Esteghlal was in the best position when the league stopped and that the request is being made legally through correspondence. He also mentioned that if they wanted to cause trouble, they would have already obtained the trophy.

The US military launched a nighttime attack targeting five Iranian oil tankers, destroying about 12% of Iran's tanker fleet within a week. The spokesperson of the Revolutionary Guards presented six new conditions from the Islamic Republic to end the war. Acceptance of these conditions by Trump was emphasized.

The Panama-flagged tanker New Andros was targeted by a drone attack in Iraqi waters and caught fire. The tanker was carrying about two million barrels of fuel oil. No casualties were reported among the 22 crew members.

A video has been released showing the Shomrud River flooding in the Malfajan rural district of Siahkal county. This incident occurred in the Malfajan rural district. Reports indicate the river has overflowed.

A citizen criticized the high price of injectable insulin pens in a video sent to Iran International. He highlighted the economic pressure on patients who cannot afford the medication. He blamed the Islamic Republic for this situation.

Donald Trump has sent a message to Tehran through Pakistani and Qatari officials that he will not return to the previous agreement between Tehran and Washington. The Pakistani army commander and Qatari delegations conveyed this message to the Islamic Republic officials. The Islamic Republic stated that it only accepts the existing agreement and is not willing to make another deal.

Mehdi Nakhl Ahmadi said the Islamic Republic wants to silence society's voice and political prisoners. He referred to Hossein Shanbehzadeh's message, who is imprisoned for placing a dot under Ali Khamenei's message. Nakhl Ahmadi also mentioned Fa'ezeh Hashemi's distortion of reality about prison.

Two weeks before the new school year begins, officials of the Islamic Republic have commented on stricter enforcement of mandatory hijab in educational centers. Gholamali Haddad Adel said that the current war conditions prevent serious engagement with the hijab issue. This topic was evaluated by Asieh Amini, a social issues analyst.

A number of Iranians gathered on Tuesday, 17 Shahrivar, in the central square of Hamburg. They protested against inflation and executions in Iran. The protesters demanded the release of political prisoners.

Benjamin Netanyahu stated during his visit to Mount Hermon that the main task is to defeat the terrorist regime of Iran and that Israel is very close to this goal. He emphasized that Israel will not allow any terrorist army to be stationed on its borders. Netanyahu also declared that Israel controls the entire area from Mount Hermon to the Mediterranean.

The spokesperson of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced the restricted area of the Islamic Republic from around Chabahar to parts of the Oman Sea and Arabian Sea. Vessels entering this area without coordination will be placed on the sanctions list. They will also be denied passage through the Strait of Hormuz.

Snapbox drivers in Semnan stopped working in protest against low fares, fuel costs, and commission rates. They announced that none of the drivers are currently working. This protest was seen in a video published on social media.

South Korea has entered a new phase of considering various options, including possible military participation against the Islamic Republic. Japan is focusing on diplomatic channels and direct talks with the Islamic Republic. These movements coincide with rising tensions in the Strait of Hormuz.

The US Department of Defense is considering scenarios for rapid amphibious operations by Marines on uninhabited Iranian islands near the Strait of Hormuz. The goal is to turn these islands into surveillance and logistical bases to protect commercial ships. The USS Tripoli, with 3,500 Marines, is present in the area, and F-35B fighters will provide air support.

On Tuesday night, with increased security measures, several government motorcycle forces were deployed in the streets of Mashhad. This was shown in a video received by Iran International. The action was taken in response to security conditions.

Ali Tajernia explained that if the transfer window does not open, the two players will stay with Aluminium until mid-season and then return to Esteghlal. Esteghlal has fulfilled its financial commitments and provided the players to Aluminium without cost. He also emphasized the importance of loyalty to commitments in football.

The Hercules Star oil tanker near Dubai experienced an incident resulting in one crew member killed and another missing. The chartering company stated that a specialized team is searching for the missing crew, and other crew members are safe. Initial assessments indicate a possible drone attack on the tanker.
A video posted on social media shows a citizen visiting the Tomb of the Immortals. The person placed flowers on their gravestone. This event has been reflected in the virtual space.

The case of 18 prisoners in Dastgerd prison in Isfahan has been referred to the Revolutionary Court. They are accused of involvement in unrest and arson at the prison. They face the risk of receiving death sentences.

Mohammad Ali Ghadousi, head of the legal department of the Football Federation, stated that managers have not yet received official notification about the indictment. The case concerns a $20,000 bonus paid to board members after qualifying for the 2022 World Cup. Yashar Soltani also reported that indictments have been issued against several senior federation managers on embezzlement charges.

A citizen stated in a video that barrels containing gasoline or oil are being transported from Mahshahr refinery to Nakja Abad by trailer. This has happened recently. No further details have been provided.
A citizen reported paying 653,000 tomans for a roll of tape and a pack of labels. This was reported via a video to Iran International. The prices of these items have significantly increased.

Bahrain's Foreign Ministry announced it will not participate in any collective meeting involving Iran until diplomatic relations are resumed. Bahrain has informed Oman of its position and considers dialogue a way to resolve disputes. It also called for the participation of all Gulf Cooperation Council countries in any agreements related to the Strait of Hormuz.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations center announced that a tanker was hit by an unknown projectile 28 nautical miles southeast of Iraq's Faw port. The tanker crew are safe and no environmental consequences have been reported so far. Authorities are investigating the incident and have urged vessels to exercise caution.

A citizen sarcastically commented in a video sent to Iran International that they are happy there is no electricity and the house is dark. He added that if they are not happy, they will be executed. This statement refers to the power outage situation.

The Iranian Foreign Ministry stated that the armed forces will respond decisively to any US aggression. This statement was issued after the US attacked several Iranian oil tankers on September 7. The ministry called these attacks a violation of international law and urged the UN Security Council to take action.

The Turkish Ministry of Foreign Affairs strongly condemned the recent Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia. Ankara warned about the threat to civilians and called for an immediate halt to the Houthis' aggressive actions. These attacks have escalated regional tensions and undermined diplomatic efforts to end the conflict in Yemen.

The police commander of Nishapur announced the closure of 13 commercial units in the city. This action was taken during the implementation of a supervisory plan. The types of violations attributed to these units were not disclosed.

Two citizens commemorated the memory of the deceased in the December 2025 protests by lighting candles for Masoud Zatparvar and Esmail Beigi Harchgani. This was done by sending videos to Iran International. These individuals are recognized as martyrs.

Sohrab Bakhtiarizadeh, head coach of Esteghlal, stated before the match against Paykan that his team aims to win three points. He mentioned the players' fatigue due to recent travels and the need to manage their energy. He also commented on the attack line and the presence of players in the youth team.

Ebrahim Rezaei stated that Iran's membership in the NPT treaty has brought no benefit and sensitive information has been exposed to espionage. He criticized the IAEA for not aiding Iran's nuclear technology and called its director a Western agent. The Islamic Republic will respond to any possible IAEA Board of Governors resolution.

A member of Iran International's editorial team referred to the Pakistani defense minister's remarks about the possible activation of the Makkah defense pact. He said the military readiness of Turkey and Pakistan to defend Saudi Arabia and the global reactions against the Houthis indicate a major decision to close the proxy conflict in Yemen.

The official funeral ceremony of Harald V, the former king of Norway, was held today in Oslo. Members of royal families and high-ranking officials from various countries attended the ceremony. Tens of thousands are expected to be present along the procession route and in central Oslo.

A member of Iran International's editorial team referred to Pakistan's defense minister's remarks about the possible activation of the Makkah defense pact. Turkey, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia are ready to support Riyadh in the war against the Houthis if the current situation in the region continues. Additionally, the recapture of Sanaa and securing the Bab al-Mandab Strait have become priorities.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations center reported an attack on a vessel 24 miles northwest of Rashid Port, Dubai. The tanker captain observed the vessel leaning, possibly due to water ingress after an unknown projectile hit. Authorities are investigating and have urged vessels to exercise caution and report suspicious activity.

Gholamali Haddad Adel stated that due to wartime conditions, the government cannot fully address the issue of hijab at the moment. He added that the influence of promoting Western lifestyle in schools is evident. He also mentioned that dealing with this issue is now more difficult than in the 1980s.

Jane Lawson has launched the "Golestan" project to create a global reference for Iranian performing arts from 1880 to 1980. This digital archive includes solo performances, plays, radio programs, and other related works. The materials are indexed and searchable by relevant keywords.

Arian Karapet, a member of the Swedish parliament, stated in an interview with Iran International that he feels obligated to support the Iranian people's demands for freedom and democratic rights. He emphasized that he speaks daily about the value of democracy in the Swedish parliament. His full interview is available on Iran International's YouTube channel.
Videos sent by citizens to Iran International show a missile passing over the skies of Abhar and Khomein in the early morning of September 8.

Brent crude oil price reached 100 dollars per barrel for the first time since early August. This price increase occurred amid ongoing conflicts in the Persian Gulf. The US announced it destroyed five oil tankers linked to the Revolutionary Guard after unsuccessful missile attacks by Iran.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the Speaker of the Parliament, addressed the US Secretary of Defense on September 8 via a Telegram post. He stated that the next target is the US energy assets in the region. This message was shared on social media.

The Islamic Republic launched a missile attack on Jordan. This attack has increased concerns about the expansion of conflict in the region. Tehran's target was a base used by American forces in Jordan.

Citizens reported the simultaneous passage of several missiles over the skies of Shahin Shahr, Najafabad, Khomeinishahr, and Baharestan. The number of missiles was reported to be between 4 and 9. The launch sites were identified as two military bases in Najafabad.

Ben Shelton defeated Carlos Alcaraz in the US Open quarterfinals to advance to the semifinals. The five-set match ended with scores of 6-7, 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, and 7-6 in favor of Shelton. Shelton will face Frances Tiafoe in the semifinals.

Pakistan has expressed its support for Saudi Arabia's right to defend its territory and citizens. The Pakistani Ministry of Foreign Affairs considers this right legitimate. This statement continues Pakistan's regional support for Saudi Arabia against proxy attacks by the Islamic Republic.

Ahmad Alavi, an economist, reported the intensification of the drug and treatment crisis in Iran. He identified the insurance budget deficit as a cause of the government's financial crisis and resource allocation issues. Financial pressure on pharmacies has led to direct treatment costs being passed to patients and the expansion of the drug black market.

Ruhollah Rahimpour stated that the CENTCOM strategic operation indicates the US is seeking to increase economic pressure on the Islamic Republic. He added that targeting Iranian oil tankers could directly pressure Iran's oil exports and foreign currency revenues.

The Iranian Football League Organization denied discrimination in dealing with teams regarding the U23 national team and considered the cancellation of Premier League matches due to the U23 team's participation in the Asian Games as in the national interest. Persepolis demanded punishment for teams that did not provide players to the U23 team. The League Organization stated that no club has privileges or restrictions outside the regulations.

Ali Faleh al-Zaydi, the Prime Minister of Iraq, agreed to Tehran's request for joint investigations regarding the discovery of drone launch pads near the border between the two countries. The investigations will be conducted jointly about the drone launch pads found near the Iraq-Iran border strip. The spokesperson for the Iraqi Armed Forces Commander-in-Chief announced this.

Lionel Messi has reached a preliminary agreement with the owners of the Spanish club Eldense to purchase the team. Eldense recently promoted to La Liga 2, and Messi intends to acquire 100% of its shares without third-party involvement. Finalizing the deal requires approval from the Spanish High Sports Council.

A citizen in a video shared on social media criticized the economic and social situation and expressed concern about the future of children in Iran. He addressed those responsible for the current situation, saying they have suffered and are worried about the children's future. This video has gained attention on social media.

Kamran Ghazanfari, a Tehran representative, said we are practically on the brink of World War III due to international tensions. He assessed the likelihood of the US using nuclear weapons against Iran as very low. He also mentioned that the plan for Iran to exit the NPT treaty might be reconsidered in parliament.

An audio file reveals that a US military aircraft warned three Iranian oil tankers that their engine rooms would be targeted for violating a military blockade. The crew was asked to leave the engine rooms within 10 minutes. US forces targeted five oil tankers linked to the IRGC.
